title: Zero-Data-Loss Private Deploy Upgrade Playbook (SRE Runbook)
author: Arjun Patel
body:
Summary:
This runbook describes a tested, operator-focused process to perform upgrades to Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments with an explicit goal: zero data loss for runtime state (KV caches, tenant snapshots, model artifacts) and minimal customer-visible disruption. It combines atomic state checkpointing, staged model activation, transactional KMS-friendly key rotation, and automated verification gates.

This 2031 revision reflects changes in tooling (snapshot v4.x), updated latency gates, and a stricter definition of “wave success” after several 2030 incident learnings.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Tenant-facing runtime components in private deployments (inference runtime, KV cache, model store, control-plane agents, local telemetry collectors).
- Not in scope: physical firmware upgrades for HW (see onprem-packaging docs) and customer-managed load balancer changes.
- Audience: SREs, field operators, deployment engineers, and delivery leads executing upgrades in customer environments.

Prerequisites and assumptions:
- Operator access to customer control plane and operator-run SSH bastion or management VPN.
- Backups of model artifacts and KV state accessible in immutable object store (S3 compatible).
- Snapshot tooling version >= 4.1.0 installed on operator workstation (replaces 3.x).
- KMS integration supports offline wrapping/unwrapping, key versions, and dual-primary “grace” windows (see KMS rotation appendix).
- Pre-approved maintenance window in calendar and customer acceptance of canary flow.
- NOTE: Starting 2031-01, “strong” KV snapshots are mandatory for tenant-critical namespaces (see KV notes).

High-level strategy (phases):
1) Validate and baseline: collect telemetry and pre-upgrade evidence.
2) Cold checkpoints: produce consistent, point-in-time snapshots of tenant runtime state.
3) Canary upgrade: upgrade control plane + 1–3 tenants with staged runtime activation and smoke tests.
4) Gradual roll: expand tenant upgrades in bounded waves with automated validation gates.
5) Switch-over: final atomic activation for remaining tenants with KV rehydrate and verification.
6) Fortify and evidence: preserve upgrade artifacts and run post-upgrade acceptance tests.

Success criteria (per wave):
- No loss of KV keys between pre-checkpoint and post-activation (0 missing keys; 0 unexpected new keys in protected namespaces).
- Latency and tail-p99 meet SLOs for canary tenants (< 140ms p50, < 450ms p99) OR match pre-upgrade baseline within configured delta (default: +10% p50, +15% p99).
- Error budget change < 3% during the wave (tightened from 5%).
- All smoke evaluation prompt-sets show no regressions beyond configured threshold.
- Snapshot restore drill remains viable: restore test of at least one tenant snapshot to a staging runtime must succeed during T-24h baseline window.

Detailed checklist and operator steps:
A. Baseline collection (T-24h to T-1h)
  1. Run auto-benchmark agent:
     `rwoodctl telemetry baseline --tenants all --duration 1h --out baseline.json`
  2. Export list of active tenants and outstanding long-lived KV sessions:
     `rwoodctl tenants list --format csv`
  3. Verify object-store snapshot health and retention window >= 96h (updated from 72h).
  4. Create pre-upgrade evidence bundle (sha256) and upload to evidence bucket.
  5. Validate KMS health and key-version visibility from the customer environment:
     `rwoodctl kms status --out kms-status.json`

B. Cold checkpoint (T-2h)
  1. Quiesce write-heavy routes: add temporary rate-limit rule for tenant hotpaths.
  2. Trigger KV checkpoint:
     `rwoodctl kv snapshot create --consistency strong --label pre-upgrade-2031-01-10`
  3. Verify snapshot completion and checksum.
  4. Export a short read-only witness token for customers that require audit proof.
  5. (New) Record snapshot manifest ID returned by snapshot v4.x (required for restore concurrency control).

C. Canary wave (T)
  1. Select 1–3 low-risk tenants (non-critical, representative workload).
  2. Upgrade control plane components (control-plane agents, operator-tools): follow package manifest install and smoke test commands in order.
  3. For each canary tenant: perform in-place runtime upgrade with staged model activation:
     - Upload new model variant to model-store with staging label `staged-<version>`
     - Start runtime in `dual-binary` mode: accept both old/new model loads but route 95% traffic to old version for 20m (reduced from 30m if gates are clean).
     - Run synthetic workload and compare outputs to golden prompt-set (automation command):
       `rwoodctl eval run --tenant TENANT_ID --prompt-set ./canary-prompts.json`
  4. If checks pass (no regressions, latency within gate), increase traffic to new model 50% for 10m, then 100%.
  5. Monitor telemetry for 60 minutes after 100% cutover before proceeding.

D. Wave expansion and throttling rules
  - Waves are timeboxed to 90 minutes each (updated from 2 hours) to reduce blast radius and improve operator focus.
  - A wave fails if any of:
    - KV drift > 0 keys in protected namespaces (auth/session/rate-limit)
    - Error rate spike > 35% over baseline for > 10 minutes (tightened)
    - P99 latency exceeds gate for > 15 minutes
    - Any KMS unwrap failure affecting model-store or snapshot envelope (now an automatic stop)
  - On failure: execute rollback for that wave (see Rollback procedures).

Rollback procedures (per-wave and final):
1. Immediate rollback trigger conditions: KV inconsistency detected, persistent tail latency degradation, KMS unwrap/rewrap failures, or customer emergency request.
2. Per-wave rollback steps:
   - Reapply older model label and switch runtime routing:
     `rwoodctl runtime route set --tenant TENANT_ID --model-label previous --force`
   - If model routing cannot be reverted within 5 minutes, trigger KV snapshot restore from `pre-upgrade` snapshot and restart runtime processes (see KV restore command below).
   - (New) If KMS rotation Phase 2 has started, pause rotation and keep old key version active; do not delete or disable any key versions.
3. Full rollback (global):
   - Pause all waves and open incident bridge (see related runbook).
   - Restore object-store model artifacts from `pre-upgrade` evidence bundle.
   - Restore KV for affected tenants:
     `rwoodctl kv snapshot restore --snapshot pre-upgrade-2031-01-10 --tenants TENANT_LIST`
   - Run full smoke regression and hold traffic behind circuit-breaker until verified.

Commands and examples:
- Create snapshot:
  `rwoodctl kv snapshot create --consistency strong --label pre-upgrade-2031-01-10 --out /tmp/snap.json`
- Restore snapshot (v4.x supports adaptive concurrency; start conservative):
  `rwoodctl kv snapshot restore --snapshot /tmp/snap.json --concurrency 2 --confirm`
- Start dual-binary runtime:
  `rwood-runtime --mode dual --old-bin /opt/runtime/v1 --new-bin /opt/runtime/v2 --health-probe /health`
- Model staging upload:
  `rwoodctl model upload --file model-1.q8 --label staged-2031-01-10`

KV and cache consistency notes:
- Always use strong-consistency checkpoints for tenant-critical KV namespaces (session tokens, auth grants, rate-limiter counters).
- Snapshot v4.x: strong-consistency snapshots may take longer but provide deterministic manifest + checksum. Plan wave timing accordingly.
- Ephemeral caches (in-memory LRU) are allowed to be warm-started; do not rely on them for correctness.
- Use the kvcmp tool to assert key-level equality for a small sample:
  `kvcmp --from snapA --to runtime --sample 1000`

KMS rotation and key versioning during upgrade:
- When upgrading components that touch key-wrapping (model-store encryption, snapshot envelopes), perform a two-phase key rotation:
  Phase 1: Add new key version as a secondary wrapping key and re-encrypt non-critical artifacts asynchronously.
  Phase 2: After successful canary and wave 1, promote new key version to primary and rewrap remaining artifacts.
- 2031 update: maintain a 14-day grace window where both old and new key versions remain enabled for unwrap operations in customer environments that may lag configuration propagation.
- Do not delete old key versions until full forensic evidence is archived and customer confirms successful acceptance.

Verification matrix (minimum checks per tenant):
| Step | Check | Command / Tool |
|------|-------|----------------|
| Pre-snapshot | Active worker count and mem pressure | `rwoodctl metrics get --worker-count` |
| Post-snapshot | Snapshot checksum matches runtime expected | `rwoodctl kv snapshot verify --snapshot /tmp/snap.json` |
| Canary outputs | Prompt-set semantic similarity >= 0.93 vs baseline (tightened) | `rwoodctl eval similarity --a baseline.json --b canary.json` |
| Post-activation | No increase in 5xx errors for 30m | `rwoodctl alerts query --metric 5xx --window 30m` |
| Post-activation | KMS unwrap error count == 0 for 30m | `rwoodctl alerts query --metric kms_unwrap_errors --window 30m` |

Roll-forward gates and sign-off:
- Waves continue only after automated gate + human sign-off from SRE on-call for restricted/private deployments.
- For large tenants (> $X revenue) also require delivery lead and customer success sign-off.
- For small tenants, automated gates suffice unless customer opted into manual approval.

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- If snapshot fails due to network timeouts: increase object-store multipart timeout and retry with concurrency 1–2.
- If model load fails with OOM: reduce max_concurrent_requests on runtime and throttle traffic; escalate to runtime team with `#runtime-ops` bridge.
- If KMS unwrap fails for a tenant: fetch secondary wrapping key and attempt offline unwrap; if unsuccessful, open high-priority support SR with KMS vendor and stop rollout.
- If post-upgrade P99 regresses but correctness is intact: hold at current wave, roll back only affected tenants, and collect heap/CPU profiles before proceeding.

Post-upgrade monitoring and evidence preservation:
- Retain evidence bundle (snapshots, checksums, logs, eval outputs) for minimum 180 days for restricted upgrades (updated from 90 days).
- Run full evaluation harness across representative prompt-sets at 1h, 6h, 24h post-upgrade.
- Update deployment manifest and chronic record in upgrade ledger:
  `rwoodctl ledger append --entry upgrade-2031-01-10 --artifact evidence-bucket/pre-upgrade-2031-01-10`

Owner and escalation matrix:
- Upgrade owner (primary): SRE On-Call (per rota)
- Runbook owner: Arjun Patel (eng-sre)
- Private deploy engineering liaison: Sofia Martinez
- Runtime/Kernel escalation: Li Wei
- Customer Success liaison: Maya Thompson

Appendix A — Sample manifest diff (text):
- runtime_image: v3.1.2 -> v3.2.0
- model_store_schema: 2030-08 -> 2031-01 (staged label defaults + stricter checksum enforcement)
- kv_snapshot_tool: 4.0.2 -> 4.1.0 (manifest IDs + improved verify)

Appendix B — Forensic checklist (mandatory for restricted upgrades):
- SHA256 of all snapshots and model artifacts
- Snapshot manifest IDs and restore logs (including concurrency settings)
- System logs from control-plane agents (window T-1h to T+2h)
- Eval outputs and similarity scores for canary tenants
- KMS key versions and rotation event log (including grace-window config)

Change history:
- 2029-02-15: Created by Sofia Martinez (initial draft)
- 2029-03-02: Added KMS rotation guidance and hardened rollback gates (reviewers: Arjun Patel, Li Wei)
- 2031-01-10: Migrated into eng-sre runbooks; tightened wave gates, retention policy, and updated snapshot tooling requirements (owner: Arjun Patel)
- 2031-02-05: Updated latency/error gates and added mandatory KMS unwrap checks; clarified v4.x snapshot manifest handling (reviewers: Priya Nair, Maya Thompson)

Related reading and references:

- See `private-deploy-evidence-preservation-and-forensic-playbook-2026` for compliance evidence retention guidelines.
- See `private-deploy-upgrade-incident-bridge-guide-2030` for incident coordination.

Contact and support:
- For immediate assistance during an upgrade, open the `#private-deploy-upgrades` channel and tag `@ops-oncall` and `@sre-oncall`.
